subject: Outbound permit narrative & evidence pack for private peering
messages:
From: BrightHealth Network Operations <netops@brighthealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private peering — outbound IP allowlisting and evidence request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. BrightHealth security needs a concise list of the outbound egress IPs your private connector will use (control plane excluded), plus the firewall policy we should apply at our perimeter NAT gateway. Our compliance team asks for: 

- A minimal allowlist of IPs with CIDR (or individual IPs) and expected port/protocols
- TTL/rotation policy for those IPs and how we'll be notified of changes
- Evidence bundle (signed doc) stating Redwood will not egress user data to third parties and retains required audit logs for 90 days
- Temporary exceptions process and an escalation contact for emergency unblocking

Can you send the above by EOD Thursday so our change window team can schedule the permit change?

Appreciate it —
Chris Park
Network Security Lead, BrightHealth
netops@brighthealth.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: BrightHealth Network Operations <netops@brighthealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private peering — outbound IP allowlisting and evidence request

Chris — thanks for the clear checklist. We can provide everything you requested; below is a concise narrative and plan so ops can validate before the change window. Full evidence pack attached once internal approvals are complete.

Key points (summary):
1) Egress footprint: Redwood private connector for BrightHealth will egress from a small set of static, customer-bound public IPv4 addresses. We provide a single CSV of canonical IPs (attached) and publish an RFC3339 effective_from timestamp on the evidence Drive link.

2) Ports/protocols:
   - 443/TCP outbound to our model-serving pool (TLS 1.2+),
   - 853/UDP for encrypted DNS (optional — see note),
   - 123/UDP NTP (outbound to their NTP pool, if allowed).

3) Rotation and notification:
   - IP rotation is rare; when required we give >=7 days notice for planned rotations via the shared Drive link and email to your netops list. Emergency changes use our on-call escalation (below) and are accompanied by signed justification.

4) Audit & retention: Redwood will supply audit logs for egress flows and control-plane requests tied to the tenant for 90 days. We will include a signed statement in the evidence bundle.

5) Exceptions & emergency unblock:
   - Primary ops contact: marissa_cole@redwood.ai (Operations Lead)
   - Escalation: oncall-inference@redwood.ai (24/7)

Action items we need from BrightHealth to proceed:
- Confirm whether BrightHealth will restrict destination FQDNs (SNI) at the NAT or only source-IP allowlist.
- Confirm whether encrypted DNS (853/UDP) is permitted; if not, we will proxy DNS over TLS via 443.

I'll loop Karthik in for the CIDR/port detail. Expect the evidence bundle by Wednesday EOD.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment stub: redwood-egress-ip-list.csv (text/csv)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: BrightHealth Network Operations <netops@brighthealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private peering — outbound IP allowlisting and evidence request

Hi Chris / team,

Technical detail from the runtime side to complement Marissa's plan:

IP set (canonical):
- 52.214.159.8/32  (control-lb, not user-data egress)
- 34.201.77.190/32 (egress-node-1)
- 34.201.77.191/32 (egress-node-2)
- 34.201.77.192/32 (egress-node-3)

We recommend you permit these exact /32 entries on your NAT outbound allowlist. The runtime will NAT customer traffic to one of the egress nodes above; we do not do arbitrary ephemeral IPs beyond this set.

Ports/protocols recommended:
- TCP/443 -> required (HTTPS to model-serving endpoints; SNI preserved)
- UDP/853 -> optional (DNS over TLS) — if blocked we will encapsulate DNS over 443
- UDP/123 -> optional (NTP); we can avoid NTP if you prefer 

Failover and fallback behavior:
- If an egress node becomes unhealthy, traffic will failover to another IP in the set.
- If all egress nodes are unreachable, client requests return a 502-like error; we will automatically trigger an incident with your oncall and provide packet-capture evidence on request.

IP rotation policy:
- Planned rotations: 7 days notice with published effective timestamp and updated CSV.
- Unplanned rotations (security incident): immediate rotation with post-facto signed incident record and 24-hour remediation window.

Evidence we will attach:
- Signed Safelist Acknowledgement (PDF)
- IP list CSV (attached)
- Export of tenant-bound audit logs (sample)
- High-level egress architecture diagram (PDF)

Let us know if BrightHealth requires CIDR aggregation or prefers listed /32s.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment stub: egress-control-design-summary.pdf (application/pdf)]
